reply.thought: I need to verify that the refunds reported by Alpha Co match the refunds recorded in my system before proceeding with payouts.
The refunds reported by Alpha Co (orders 192 and 193) match the refunds recorded in my system. I can now proceed to calculate the net balance for each customer.

The net_balance tool returned an error indicating that customer '192' does not exist. This suggests that the order ID 192 may correspond to a different customer, or there is a mismatch in the data. I need to investigate further to identify the correct customer associated with the refunds.

I have the list of orders. Order 192 belongs to customer 'cobalt' and order 193 belongs to customer 'acme'. I need to compute the net balance for each customer by subtracting the refunds from their total order amounts. Then I will record the payouts. First, I'll get the net balance for customer 'cobalt'.
I have the net balance for customer  'cobalt' (18779 cents). Now I need the net balance for customer  'acme'.
I have the net balance for customer 'acme' (33841 cents). Next, I need the net balance for customer 'birch'.
I have the net balances for all customers: cobalt (18779 cents), acme (33841 cents), and birch (40664 cents). Now I will record the payouts for each customer.
The payout for customer 'cobalt' has been recorded successfully. Next, I will record the payout for customer 'acme'.

The payout for customer 'acme' has been recorded successfully. Now I will record the payout for customer 'birch'.
All payouts have been recorded successfully. I will now finish the batch and report the payouts.
